title: Project D — Production Backend (Rust vs Express)
summary: Implement the same order-management API twice — once in Rust (axum-style layering) and once in Express — then compare them honestly across architecture, error handling, concurrency, observability, testing and operational characteristics.
requirements: Same REST contract in both implementations (OpenAPI shared): create order, list orders (cursor pagination), get by id, health/readiness
Both use the layered architecture: transport / application / domain / infrastructure
Both validate input at the boundary with structured error responses (one error envelope)
Idempotency-Key handling on create in both
Both instrumented: structured logs with request ids + RED metrics endpoint
Both tested: unit tests for the service layer with faked repositories; HTTP-level tests for the contract
Graceful shutdown implemented in both (drain in-flight, bounded)
A COMPARISON REPORT: concurrency model, error ergonomics, type safety, performance observations, ops story — with evidence, not vibes

hints: Write the OpenAPI contract first and generate review checklists from it — the comparison is only fair if both implement the same thing.
Keep the domain layer identical in spirit (same rules, same names) so differences you measure are the stack, not the design.
Use the same load script (e.g. 200 concurrent, 60s) against both; record p50/p95 and memory, not impressions.
completionCriteria: Both implementations pass the same HTTP-level contract tests
Both implement idempotent create + graceful shutdown
Load-test numbers recorded for both under identical conditions
Comparison report fills every matrix row with evidence
